_comment: Athlete-language symptom index for kick_chat: maps what an athlete SAYS ('the ball keeps popping up on me') to the documented mechanics behind it, the fault families whose deterministic signatures may confirm it (ids from kick_fault_cue_map.json), and the specific metric rows to inspect in the computed athlete-vs-pro table (frameKey.metricId, side in parentheses where it matters). This file routes attention; it never decides. The model must check which candidateFaults actually appear in faultScreen.candidates and what the cited rows show for THIS rep before blaming any mechanism. dataLimits entries are honesty requirements, not hedges — when the listed limit applies, say plainly that our side-on camera cannot measure it.

athleteLanguage: ball goes up in the air when I don't want it to
symptoms.mechanics: Launch angle is set by where the instep meets the ball and the direction the foot is travelling through contact. The ball balloons when the strike lands below the ball's centre with the foot still travelling upward, which happens when the plant foot is behind the ball (the instep tilts up and reaches under it), when the weight/COM hangs back at contact (trunk tipped away from the target beyond the pro's backward lean), or when the last step is so long the athlete is leaning back to reach the ball at all.
symptoms.dataLimits: Ball contact lasts roughly 10 ms — about two frames at 240 fps — so the exact contact point on the ball's surface is inferred from foot-vs-ball offsets, never measured directly.
symptoms.askIfUnclear: Does it happen on every kick, or mostly when you're going for power?

symptoms.mechanics: Ball speed is governed by foot speed at contact and the quality of the strike, and foot speed comes from proximal-to-distal sequencing: thigh rotates first, then the shank whips through late. Weak shots trace to a shallow backswing (little knee flexion to accelerate through), broken sequencing (shank peaks before or with the thigh instead of after), or simply low foot speed for the athlete's stature. Plant-foot fore-aft position is NOT a power lever — a ±15 cm shift showed no significant effect on ball velocity — so never sell plant placement as the power fix.
symptoms.dataLimits: Ankle rigidity at impact matters for the strike but is not resolvable at our frame rate; coach it by feel (firm, locked-down ankle), not by number.
symptoms.askIfUnclear: Is it weak even when you catch it cleanly, or mostly on mishits?

symptoms.mechanics: The mirror image of ballooning: the strike lands at or above the ball's centre with the mass already over it. A plant foot well ahead of the ball puts the knee and chest over the strike and caps the launch angle, and a trunk pitched toward the target at contact does the same.
symptoms.dataLimits: If the athlete WANTS a low driven ball, a slightly-ahead plant and forward lean are correct technique — ask what they're trying to hit before 'fixing' this.
symptoms.askIfUnclear: Are you trying to keep it down, or trying to lift it and it won't go?

symptoms.mechanics: Repeatable accuracy needs a repeatable strike, and the two measurable anchors are plant-foot placement (fore-aft position governs trajectory far more than speed) and a quiet, balanced trunk through contact. Pinned or crossed arms remove the counterbalance that keeps the pelvis stable, which shows up as scatter rather than one consistent miss.
symptoms.dataLimits: Side-to-side plant distance from the ball and where the foot meets the ball laterally are invisible to our side-on camera — if the misses are consistently left or right, say we can't measure that directly and coach the repeatable-strike anchors we can see.
symptoms.askIfUnclear: Do the misses go one way (always left, always right, always high), or scatter everywhere?

athleteLanguage: ball curls when I don't want it to
symptoms.mechanics: Unwanted curve is sidespin from striking the ball off-centre laterally or with an open/closed foot face — none of which a single sagittal camera can measure. Be honest about that. What we can sanity-check is the sagittal setup that makes a square strike easier: plant placement and hip-openness at contact compared to the pro.
symptoms.dataLimits: Lateral contact offset and foot-face angle have no detectable signature in a sagittal view — never claim to see the cause of curve in this data. Ask which way it bends and coach strike-surface feel (bone of the laces, toes down and locked).
symptoms.askIfUnclear: Which way does it curve — toward your kicking side or across your body?

symptoms.mechanics: Clean contact needs the foot to arrive at the ball in a repeatable position. A kicking knee already near-straight before contact means the athlete is reaching — the foot arrives at the end of its arc where small timing errors become big contact errors — and weight hanging back moves the whole strike zone. Head/eye position matters too but is not in our data.
symptoms.dataLimits: Toe-vs-laces contact on the ball's surface is inferred from foot-centre offsets, not observed; frame the evidence as 'the numbers suggest', not 'I can see'.
symptoms.askIfUnclear: Where on your foot do you feel it hit — toe, laces, or inside?

athleteLanguage: I fall over after I kick
symptoms.mechanics: The support leg absorbs and holds the whole action: a collapsing support knee lets the pelvis drop mid-strike, pinned arms remove the counter-rotation that keeps the trunk quiet, and weight left behind the ball forces a rescue step after contact. Some forward travel after a maximal strike is normal — compare against the pro before calling it a fault.
symptoms.dataLimits: A single rep can't separate a balance habit from one awkward strike — if only this rep shows it, say so and suggest checking it across a few reps.
symptoms.askIfUnclear: Does it happen on every kick or only when you swing at 100%?

symptoms.mechanics: SAFETY ROUTE — not a technique conversation. Kicking-related pain in a growing athlete can involve the hip flexor/AIIS (avulsion risk in adolescents), the front of the knee (Osgood-Schlatter territory), the groin, or the lower back. None of these should be coached through.
symptoms.dataLimits: Pose data cannot assess injury. Do not offer a technique fix, a workaround, or a 'kick softer' compromise as if it resolves the issue.
symptoms.askIfUnclear: Where exactly does it hurt, and does it hurt during the kick or after?
symptoms.response: Tell them to stop repetitive maximal kicking until it's been looked at, to tell their coach or parent, and to see a qualified professional (physio or doctor). Be warm and brief; do not diagnose.

noMatchGuidance: If the complaint matches no entry, reason from kick_biomechanics.md's phase model and the computed athlete-vs-pro deltas: find the phase the complaint lives in, check the rep's largest confident deviations there, and answer from those. If the complaint is about something our sagittal view cannot measure, say so plainly rather than improvising.
